name: Far-right politics
summary: Far-right politics sits to the right of the mainstream right and combines ultranationalism, authoritarianism and nativism, the view that the state belongs to the native group. It stresses order, hierarchy, traditional family and national culture, and opposes immigration, multiculturalism, communism and supranational bodies. Scholars split it into an extreme right that rejects democracy and a radical right that works through elections while rejecting liberal pluralism.
scope: The mainstream populist radical right as it exists today in Europe and beyond, following Cas Mudde's nativism-authoritarianism-populism core and the Sweden Democrats' programme as one stated example. Extreme-right and fascist strands, which are more revolutionary, racial and violent, appear as notes and as zeroes where they split from the mainstream. Fascism and right-wing populism have separate profiles.

sources.title: Radical right (Europe)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Welfare chauvinism, Euroscepticism, economic divisions among parties, democracy and Islam.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Parties split between welfare-state and free-market lines; the Sweden Democrats back tax-funded care, others do not.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Blue-collar and small-business wings of the radical right pull in opposite directions on state intervention in wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Some parties lean free-market and others state-interventionist; no shared line, and the Swedish programme calls for a regulated market economy.

public-ownership.rationale: Mainstream radical-right parties accept private ownership, though extra-parliamentary groups favour more state control; inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Not a defining issue; most parties favour business-friendly taxation while stressing national solidarity, so this is an inference.

unions-good.rationale: Attitudes range from the Swedish programme's defence of the labour-market model to hostility toward unions on the extreme right.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Swedish programme calls property rights a necessary condition for social progress; other strands share the view.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-elite rhetoric targets economic elites, but parties diverge between deregulation and state direction.

cut-welfare.rationale: The distinctive position is welfare chauvinism, restricting benefits to nationals, not cutting welfare as such; the Swedish programme defends a generous welfare model.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is a left-wing idea; the family favours class collaboration, so this is inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security fears and a law-and-order outlook lead the family to favour giving authorities wider powers.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Mudde notes authoritarians treat drug addiction as a criminal matter to be punished.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Parties often resist hate-speech laws as censorship, though European ones moderate their image under such laws.

strong-leader.rationale: Authoritarianism, a belief in strict order and obedience, is a core element; extreme-right strands go further.

state-harmful.rationale: The family treats the state as the guardian of the nation and of order, so abolitionism is alien to it.

limit-guns.rationale: No common line: US far-right groups defend gun rights while European parties usually accept strict regimes.

empower-police-military.rationale: Law and order is a defining pillar; the Swedish programme asks for more resources and powers for police and border forces.

decide-locally.rationale: The emphasis falls on the unified nation; Vox-style parties oppose regional autonomy. Inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the family's treatment of perceived sexual deviancy as an authoritarian concern.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Swedish programme puts victims first and wants quick, consistent punishment; authoritarianism favours punishment over support.

traditional-family.rationale: Traditional family, hierarchy and social roles are listed as defining positions; the Swedish programme calls the family the basic community.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The family is described as antifeminist and anti-LGBT with a traditional-family outlook, though some Western parties are softer.

abortion-legal.rationale: Traditional-family values point against, but positions vary and sources say little on abortion; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religious nationalism or a national religion recurs; the Swedish programme says the state should not be religiously neutral and gives Christianity a special place.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Race-conscious redress conflicts with the in-group, ethnically defined view of the nation.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Antifeminism and traditional gender hierarchy are listed principles.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defence of national identity and culture is central; the Swedish programme calls culture the basis of the nation's survival.

gradual-change.rationale: Radical-right parties often invoke tradition, but revolutionary and national-rebirth strands reject gradualism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Closing borders and cutting immigration is the central policy of nativism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Opposition to globalism and supranational bodies is shared; the Swedish programme accepts only intergovernmental cooperation.

free-trade.rationale: Economic nationalism and anti-globalism are common, though the Swedish programme is basically pro-free trade with exceptions.

nation-first.rationale: Ultranationalism puts national interest first; the Swedish programme wants an independent foreign policy centred on national interests.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-globalism and sovereignty emphasis weigh against interventions for human rights; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Closed borders are a core nativist aim, and the Swedish programme calls for strictly limited migration.

limit-growth.rationale: The Swedish programme treats growth as necessary, balanced against heritage and environment; inferred for the family.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is not a defining theme; parties generally resist costly state-led climate measures. Inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented shared line; romantic and technophile strands both exist.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The Swedish programme backs nuclear power as a base of electricity supply; other parties vary.

revolution-justified.rationale: Extreme-right groups can be revolutionary while radical-right parties work through elections.

experts-over-public.rationale: Populism contrasts the people with corrupt, anti-national elites, which includes experts.

central-planning.rationale: Most parties favour a market economy; only some extra-parliamentary groups favour state control. Inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Worker or public ownership is not part of the family; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the family; inferred from the property-rights emphasis.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Family continuity and property rights suggest opposition; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Rights-and-duties welfare morality opposes unconditional payments; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Anti-globalism and economic nationalism often lead to protectionism, though some parties favour free trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Corporatism and state control of some sectors are documented, though free-market parties differ.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Agrarian and small-business strands favour widespread small ownership; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing wages is a communist aim, opposed by the family's anti-communism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Swedish programme wants an independent national central bank; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Corporatism is documented in fascist and extreme-right strands but not in the radical-right mainstream.

one-party-rule.rationale: Extreme-right strands accept it, but radical-right parties accept elections and pluralism of parties.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Maurras-style royalists and the Swedish programme accept monarchy, while fascist and republican strands do not.

democracy-best.rationale: Mudde places the radical right as accepting democracy while rejecting minority rights and the rule of law; the extreme right rejects popular sovereignty.

direct-votes.rationale: Populism favours direct popular rule, and the Swedish programme wants stronger direct democracy.

workers-councils.rationale: A council-based order is socialist; the far right is anti-communist.

right-to-secede.rationale: Territorial unity of the nation is stressed, as in Vox's opposition to Catalan autonomy; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Organicism and hierarchy are documented, including an 'organic oligarchy' in some strands.

political-violence-never.rationale: Extreme-right movements endorse violence while radical-right parties generally disavow it.

war-builds-character.rationale: Militarism features in extreme-right and fascist strands but not in the mainstream radical right.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religious nationalism is common; the Swedish programme says the state cannot be religiously neutral.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Theocratic strands exist, but most adherents favour religion as heritage rather than as a legal source.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Security is treated as the state's foremost task.

military-superiority.rationale: The military is seen as the final guarantor of national self-determination; ultranationalism supports strength.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nativism holds that states should belong to the native group, and ethnic nationalism is a documented core.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Organicism treats society as a unified whole, against class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy and the rejection of egalitarianism are central.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on state sovereignty over the national territory.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Ultranationalism rejects guilt-based claims on the nation's resources; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Some strands favour civilisational blocs, though the Swedish programme stresses intergovernmental ties.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collective duty is stressed, but economic strands vary.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Swedish programme ties rights to duties, and organicism puts the community first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Blood-and-soil roots and animal and nature care appear, so a mild yes; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Concern about native decline and support for families lead against limiting population; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Some romantic strands lament modernity, but the mainstream does not; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Only accelerationist fringes want disruption; the mainstream stresses preservation. Inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anti-elite populism and a preference for popular sovereignty point against; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Security fears and law-and-order views point toward state access; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Ultraconservatism, reaction and calls for national rebirth set a lost order above progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Mudde notes parties mix ideological rigidity and pragmatism, adapting to voters while keeping nativism.

direct-action.rationale: Radical-right parties work through elections; direct action is mainly an extra-parliamentary approach.

means-match-ends.rationale: No documented commitment to prefiguration; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No strand of the family advocates it; inferred.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A communist aim opposed by the family.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is communist; the Swedish programme still ties rewards to work.

production-for-use.rationale: Not a family theme; the Swedish programme backs a regulated market economy; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Class-exploitation theory conflicts with class collaboration and organicism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Radical anti-communism is a defining feature.

collective-farming.rationale: Anti-communism and agrarian small-property traditions oppose it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Some anti-capitalist strands blame finance, but the mainstream does not endorse the Marxist thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Swedish programme says taxes must fund a strong welfare; inferred for the family.

harm-principle.rationale: Authoritarianism favours restricting conduct seen as deviant or disorderly, beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Organicism and ethnically defined peoples give weight to group belonging; minority rights are rejected.

conscription.rationale: The Swedish programme backs general conscription, a view shared by authoritarian, militarist strands.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Populism prizes popular control of the state; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is treated as the national guardian rather than a business; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Swedish programme stresses material security for compatriots while other strands do not.

media-academia-power.rationale: Populist anti-elite rhetoric casts media and cultural elites as corrupting the people; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racist strands endorse it, but radical-right parties mostly use cultural arguments.

organic-representation.rationale: Organicism and corporatism appear in some strands, while parties compete in elections.

total-state.rationale: Fascist strands endorse total control but the mainstream does not.

national-rebirth.rationale: Calls for national rebirth against decadence are a documented theme, especially in revolutionary strands.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Irredentist strands exist, but the Swedish programme recognises equal rights of all nations.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oath-based rule is not part of the family.

universal-morality.rationale: Traditionalists and religious nationalists claim moral truth but stress particular cultures; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Organicism treats the nation as one homogeneous whole with a single interest.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Antisemitism is central to many strands while others of the family are pro-Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Ethnic nationalism supports co-ethnic return, as in Hungary; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language is part of the national identity, but not a stated priority; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not part of the family; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Swedish programme allows private providers; other parties have no shared line.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Swedish programme prefers sound finances; other parties differ.

rule-by-example.rationale: Authoritarianism favours law, order and punishment.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-rule for the nation is a core claim and the Swedish programme says all nations hold the right.

force-without-un.rationale: The Swedish programme wants UN-sanctioned missions, whereas other strands are unilateralist.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religious nationalism and romanticism do not subscribe; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare chauvinism is a documented core element.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Swedish programme ties rights to duties; Mudde notes a punitive view of unemployment.

class-collaboration.rationale: Organicism holds that social classes belong together as one nation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The family defends heritage and tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: Some strands (Dugin) favour an anti-Western front, while others side with the West.

workers-nation.rationale: The Swedish programme stresses solidarity on national rather than class lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Patriarchy and traditional roles are listed principles.

ban-interest.rationale: Anti-finance themes appear in some strands, but a ban is not the mainstream.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Ethnopluralism and separation of groups appear, but explicit racial legal classification is a fringe position among radical-right parties.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The family rejects Marxist class analysis and treats the state as the nation's institution.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not a defining issue; the family tends to favour national energy supply over costly transition measures, so this is inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nativist programmes such as the Sweden Democrats' expect newcomers to adopt the national culture rather than keep their own.

elite-replacement.rationale: Replacement narratives are common in the wider far right and tied to nativism, but the mainstream radical right often avoids or denies the deliberate-plot claim; inferred from the nativist core.

proportional-representation.rationale: Radical-right parties use both systems and the profile's sources state no common position, so adherents are split.

national-mission.rationale: Nativism and national self-determination point inward, to protecting the nation rather than exporting its system; inferred, not stated.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The far right stresses traditional family and distinct roles and rejects the view that society systematically disadvantages women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The populist element of the radical right casts politicians as a corrupt elite set against the pure people.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic ideas appear on the extreme right, but the mainstream radical right in this scope does not advocate them; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Given its law-and-order stress and support for police and military, an adherent would resist prosecuting past security-force conduct; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Far-right programmes favour a strong state for order and welfare for citizens, not a minimal one; inferred from those positions.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Extreme-right strands want racial separation, but the mainstream radical right frames its case in cultural and national terms and does not call for discouraging mixed marriage; inferred from its nativism.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Nativism and hierarchy lead the far right to reject equal moral worth across groups, though radical-right parties accept equal legal rights for citizens; inferred from the nativist core.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not an issue the far right addresses; socialism is opposed anyway, so the statement offers no purchase and the strand is treated as indifferent.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nativist parties see the nation as belonging to its native group and resist framing their own states as colonial projects; inferred from that nativism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Radical-right parties generally oppose separate religious legal regimes for minorities and want one national law; inferred from their opposition to multiculturalism.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Parties differ: some defend a national religion's position, while others, like the Swedish programme, accept religious freedom as a liberal-democratic right.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian issue outside the European radical right scope; it has no shared position.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Parties split between defending the national religious heritage in schools and secular state schooling aimed at minority religions.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine about socialist states that the far right does not address.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The radical right claims to speak for the will of the people and works through elections, but the extreme right rejects democratic legitimacy; inferred from Mudde's populism core.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred from the populist distrust of elites, media and academia as serving their own interests.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the economic nationalism and 'own people first' stress.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred: nativism and calls for repatriation and remigration are common, though the mainstream radical right frames them as incentives.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Inferred: the authoritarian strand accepts force for order and national goals.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred from the hierarchy and national-struggle themes common to the far right.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Split: parties ban communists and extremists in principle but are often themselves targets of such bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred: it emphasises collective and national belonging over individual non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred: the authoritarian and populist core favours decisive majority or leader power over checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred: it relies on mass nationalist movements and elections, not a revolutionary vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred: nativist 'welfare chauvinism' puts native citizens first, not the poor as such.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Welfare-chauvinist and free-market parties of the radical right differ on state housing, so there is no shared line.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Order-focused authoritarianism favours limits on disruptive action, but blue-collar wings of the radical right support unions; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The radical right blames elites and immigration, not population growth, but some strands hold Malthusian views; no shared line.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Organicism and nativism hold that a state should belong to a people sharing ancestry and culture, and that non-natives threaten homogeneity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The far right stresses hierarchy and elite leadership and the radical right works through elections, so selection by lottery runs against it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarianism stresses order and strong measures against enemies; the radical right works within electoral law, so adherents differ.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Economic views split between free-market and interventionist parties, so there is no shared line on price ceilings.

party-controls-media.rationale: Authoritarian strands favour control of information, but the radical right works through elections and complains of media bias and censorship; split.

party-commands-army.rationale: Extreme-right strands favour party or leader command of the army while radical-right parties accept the constitutional state; split.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Nativism favours making citizenship hard to get and tied to assimilation; no single residence period is stated.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred: the far right rarely addresses officials' pay and its populist strand attacks elite perks, but it does not demand wage-parity for office, which is a left-egalitarian idea.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred: authoritarian movements demand discipline, but radical-right parties working through elections generally allow free votes, so the strands split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Opposition to supranational bodies such as the EU is a defining far-right position; the Sweden Democrats' programme rejects handing sovereignty to a union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian core and the preference for strong executives; radical-right parties in parliamentary systems often accept legislative control.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred: religious-nationalist strands favour hierarchical national churches, but secular and populist strands are indifferent to church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred: the far right values religion as national heritage but seeks rule by the nation's leaders, not clergy; theocratic rule is a fringe position.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Ultranationalism puts loyalty to the nation first, so working for one's own government's defeat is the opposite of the far-right view.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on traditional values and national culture; radical-right parties often seek to restrict art seen as degenerate or anti-national.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: authoritarian-leaning movements tend to back long-serving leaders chosen by voters, though electoral radical-right parties do not campaign on this.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: populist strands favour direct accountability to the people against elites, but authoritarian strands distrust such controls, so adherents split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Radical-right parties are Eurosceptic and oppose supranational bodies, but many back NATO and strong national defence, so adherents are split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Hierarchy, property and national tradition are central; abolishing rentals is a left-egalitarian idea, so the answer is inferred as strong opposition.

people-in-arms.rationale: Such parties favour strong national defence, often with conscription, rather than abolishing a professional army; an armed-citizenry plank is inferred as unlikely.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Organic, traditionalist views of the nation tend to idealise rural and peasant roots; inferred from organicism.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Ultranationalism commonly supports uniting ethnic nations divided by borders; inferred from that strand, with some mainstream parties silent on it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Mudde's account of populism and anti-elite conspiracies describes elites as detached from the 'pure people', which includes the educated class.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nativism and a defence of a particular national culture are core, and the programme ranks assimilation to the national culture above cultural equality.

death-penalty.rationale: Law-and-order authoritarianism favours harsh punishment; capital punishment itself varies by country and party, so the answer is inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The traditional-family emphasis suggests opposition to gender-equality teaching in schools; inferred, with sex education itself less contested.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious traditionalists on the far right may favour it, but secular nationalist parties do not; adherents are split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: A traditional-family and national-culture stance supports restricting pornography; inferred rather than stated.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nativism holds that the state belongs to the native group, which implies citizenship by descent over birthright.

minority-language-support.rationale: The programme favours assimilation to the national language and culture, so it does not back extra support for minority languages, although indigenous or historic minorities may be exceptions.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Opposition to Islam and multiculturalism implies resistance to exemptions for religious minorities; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Emphasis on order, hierarchy and national conformity implies discouraging eccentricity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist priority on the native group; the radical right distrusts spending national wealth or forgiving debts for foreigners, but it rarely addresses this.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Strands differ: nativists want national control of the economy, while many radical-right parties accept the market; inferred as split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Radical-right parties often favour popular votes but the extreme right rejects democracy; adherents are split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian core, which prizes order over liberal pluralism, though development is rarely the stated reason.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Welfare and aid are put first for 'our own people'; the programme-style slogan favours compatriots over foreigners.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from ultranationalism and the stress on national sovereignty and strong defence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Populist strands favour direct election while authoritarian and monarchist strands do not; adherents are split.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Radical-right populists criticise unelected technocrats while market-minded parties back independent banks; adherents are split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from ultranationalism, which treats the national homeland as non-negotiable.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Some strands support a national or organic view of property while others defend market property; the ideology is split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anti-communist but with no settled view on how to classify the USSR; the question is not one the ideology addresses.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from radical-right hostility to costly climate and environmental regulation and to supranational rule-making; some parties stress nature conservation, so not -2.

collective-defense.rationale: Radical-right parties split between Atlanticist, NATO-supporting ones and Euroscepticist or Russia-friendly ones that reject binding alliances; the Sweden Democrats back defence cooperation.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Adherents divide: nationalists condemn annexations of their own lands, while others accept conquest or Russian annexations; no common doctrine.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from the radical right's defence of national religious heritage and traditional institutions; it rarely seeks to curb church property, though some secular strands accept state control of Islam.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from organic nationalism, which casts the head of state as embodying the nation; strands favouring strongman or elected presidents would dissent.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Ultranationalism treats national unity and territorial integrity as paramount, so adherents typically accept force to keep the state whole.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from nativist insistence on a single national culture, law and order; regional autonomy is accepted mainly by regionalist parties.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Mainstream radical right is secular-democratic in form and does not ascribe divinity to rulers; only some extreme-right and traditionalist strands do.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Parties split on economics: free-market radical-right parties favour flat taxes, welfare-chauvinist ones defend the existing system.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from organicist and nativist views that national character and ability are inherited and rooted in descent; mainstream radical right stresses culture and assimilation, so not -2.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Radical-right parties work through elections and claim to defend the rule of law, though they favour strong executives; the extreme right would say yes.

space-expansion.rationale: The topic is not part of the radical-right program; adherents are indifferent or split between nationalist prestige and spending priorities at home.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not a theme of the far right; its strands range from populist direct rule by the people to hierarchical elite rule.

leader-cult.rationale: Extreme-right strands venerate the leader, but the mainstream radical right in democracies avoids formal cults of personality.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-family emphasis, which is cross-pressured by fathers' rights appeals and by traditional views of mothers as primary carers.

missingStatements.text: Immigrants should be expected to give up their original culture and assimilate into the national culture.
missingStatements.rationale: The Swedish programme makes assimilation its alternative to multiculturalism, and Mudde says nativists want non-natives to assimilate or leave.

missingStatements.text: Elites are deliberately promoting mass immigration to replace or weaken the native population.
missingStatements.rationale: Mudde describes the far right framing mass immigration as a plot by progressive elites, and the far-right literature records replacement conspiracies as central to some strands.

notes: Extreme-right strands (fascist, neo-Nazi, white supremacist) answer more extremely on race, violence, democracy and the state; radical-right parties differ on economics, from free-market to welfare-state. Answers of 0 mark real splits among these strands.
